title: Felix and the Ghost
premise: Emrys Delacroix, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained loss of her family aboard Flight 4471, is assigned a case that officially does not exist: a passenger jet whose records vanish mid-flight while the aircraft is still airborne. Following a trail of erased manifests and ghost-trained pilots, she uncovers 'the Ghost' — a covert network that trains and launders rogue aviators for hire — and discovers it was responsible for her family's flight. With help from a defected Ghost handler named Ilya and a makeshift crew of outcasts who become her found family, Emrys races to expose the network before its operatives scatter at a shifting border checkpoint. In the end she burns the Ghost's training hub to the ground, chooses love and loyalty over the duty that failed her, and finally lets row twelve rest.
about_author: Lena Kavanagh is a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reviewing accident reports before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people who seek justice in the gaps the law leaves behind.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Opening on the anniversary of Flight 4471, she visits the crash archive and touches the sealed file of row twelve, where her family sat. Establishes her grief-fueled precision and her rule: never take cases with living relatives. Emotional beat: controlled sorrow masking rage.

chapters.title: The Case That Isn't
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Her supervisor hands her a folder for Meridian Air 88, a flight currently in the air whose booking records, crew files, and transponder history have all just evaporated from every database. Officially, the flight doesn't exist. Beat: cold dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Still in the Air
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She tracks the phantom aircraft via an air traffic friend's private logs — it landed two hours ago at a regional strip, then vanished again. Eleven survivors walked off and dispersed. Beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Ilya Petrov
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. A former handler for a network called the Ghost watches news of Meridian 88 and knows his old trainees were aboard. He burns his own safehouse and goes dark. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Survivor One
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She finds a survivor, Dana Okafor, hiding in a freight yard. Dana describes a mid-flight announcement: 'This flight never happened. Cooperate and you land.' Beat: fear becoming testimony.

chapters.title: The Training Manual
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya retrieves a hidden copy of the Ghost's training doctrine — how they manufacture untraceable pilots. He decides Emrys, the investigator asking loud questions, is either his weapon or his death sentence. Beat: calculated risk.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ilya approaches Emrys in a parking garage with proof: the Ghost trained the crew of her family's flight too. She nearly arrests him; instead she listens. Beat: hatred meeting necessity.

chapters.title: What the Files Say
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Cross-referencing Ilya's manual against old reports, she finds the Ghost's signature in three 'unsolvable' crashes — including 4471. Beat: grief detonating into purpose.

chapters.title: The Crew Assembles
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Emrys gathers her unlikely team: Dana the survivor, Theo a disgraced radio tech, and Marisol a records clerk who can forge anything. None of them are family; all of them become one. Beat: warmth kindling inside the thriller engine.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Geography
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The team maps the border checkpoint where Ghost operatives funnel south — and learns the guard rotations shift in nine days. Their window is fixed. Beat: ticking clock installed.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Flashback chapter: Ilya's years inside the Ghost, training pilots to disappear, until a trainee he loved was used on a job he couldn't stomach. Beat: shame as backstory, sympathy earned.

chapters.title: Meridian 88's Real Cargo
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The vanished flight wasn't carrying passengers — it carried the Ghost's ledger, smuggled in the hold. Someone on board stole it. Beat: the MacGuffin revealed.

chapters.title: The Thief
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana admits she took pages of the ledger during the chaos of landing. She's been running ever since. Beat: betrayal inside the found family.

chapters.title: Pages of Names
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The stolen pages list paid jobs — including a payment dated the week of Flight 4471. Proof, but incomplete without the master ledger. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The team realizes their communications are compromised when a forged record comes back annotated by the Ghost itself. Beat: paranoia tightening the screws.

chapters.title: Burn the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Action chapter, alternating POV. The Ghost raids their safehouse; the team escapes through service tunnels with seconds to spare, losing their physical evidence. Beat: first major loss.

chapters.title: Duty Calls
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Her agency suspends her for pursuing a non-existent case and offers reinstatement if she walks away. Duty versus justice crystallizes. Beat: the institutional door closing.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Emrys and Ilya, shared POV. On a rooftop, grief and attraction finally speak plainly. Ilya offers her an exit; she refuses — but not alone anymore. Beat: the romance consummated emotionally, not physically.

chapters.title: The Handler's Handler
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya identifies Voss, the Ghost's director, whom even Ilya never met face-to-face. One name, no face, seven days until the checkpoint shift. Beat: the antagonist acquires a shape.

chapters.title: Trap Bait
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The team leaks false ledger pages to draw Voss's cleaners into the open. It works too well — they capture Theo. Beat: plan curdling into cost.

chapters.title: Exchange
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A prisoner swap at a rail yard goes wrong; Dana takes a bullet shielding Emrys. They keep Theo, lose the element of surprise. Beat: sacrifice binding the family tighter.

chapters.title: Hospital Vigil
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. While Dana fights for her life, Marisol forges the team's way past federal watchlists. Quiet chapter, deepening bonds. Beat: tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: Voss Unmasked
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Following money, not faces, Emrys unmasks Voss: a respected aviation safety board member — the man who signed off on closing her family's case. Beat: personal devastation weaponized.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss meets Emrys openly, offering truth, restitution, and 4471's full file — if she returns the stolen pages and disappears. He shows her a photo proving her family's death was collateral, not target. Beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys reads her family's true file alone, weeps once, and burns Voss's offer. Justice outside the law becomes her only law. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Four Days
chapters.summary: Team POV mosaic. Countdown logistics: forged credentials, a hijacked freight schedule, Ilya's knowledge of the checkpoint's blind spots. Beat: coiled readiness.

chapters.title: Ghost Hub
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya reveals the training hub's location — a decommissioned air base where the Ghost manufactures its pilots. The master ledger is there. So are the simulators. Beat: destination locked.

chapters.title: Infiltration Plan
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, recovered and sharp. The team plans a two-pronged strike: Emrys and Ilya inside for the ledger, Marisol and Theo triggering the checkpoint chaos outside. Beat: strategy as suspense.

chapters.title: Last Normal Night
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Dinner in a borrowed farmhouse; stories about the families they lost and found. Emrys almost tells Ilya she loves him. Beat: calm before the storm, earned warmth.

chapters.title: The Hub
chapters.summary: Emrys and Ilya POV. They infiltrate the air base at night, moving through hangars full of stripped fuselages — including one painted with 4471's livery, used for training. Beat: horror in a familiar shape.

chapters.title: Ledger in Hand
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys secures the master ledger and finds Voss waiting — unarmed, confident, certain she'll trade. She records his confession instead. Beat: checkmate attempted.

chapters.title: Alarm
chapters.summary: Action, alternating POV. The Ghost's security floods the hangar; Ilya holds a corridor alone so Emrys can run. Beat: love proven in gunfire.

chapters.title: Fire
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Cornered, Emrys ignites the fuel depot, burning the hub and the simulator where her family's final flight was rehearsed. She carries the ledger out through smoke. Beat: catharsis through destruction.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Shift
chapters.summary: Marisol and Theo POV. At the border, the shift changes early; the team's window collapses. Marisol bluffs a convoy through on forged papers as sirens rise behind them. Beat: peak external tension.

chapters.title: Ilya's Choice
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Wounded, Ilya is captured covering the escape — and gives Voss's name to the one honest federal agent Emrys trusts, choosing justice over self-preservation. Beat: sacrifice completing his arc.

chapters.title: Ledger to the Light
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys distributes the ledger to press, victims' families, and prosecutors simultaneously — beyond anyone's power to bury. Voss's network unravels publicly within hours. Beat: justice executed outside and then through the law.

chapters.title: Voss Falls
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Voss arrested at his own safety-board podium; Ilya released pending testimony; the checkpoint operation rolls up forty operatives. Beat: the machine broken.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Reopened
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The 4471 case is formally reopened; names restored to the record. Emrys reads her family's names aloud at the hearing, steady-voiced. Beat: grief given dignity.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Weeks later: Dana walking again, Theo rebuilding radios, Marisol forging nothing but birthday cards. The team keeps meeting anyway — Sundays, always. Beat: warmth as resolution.

chapters.title: Felix and the Ghost
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys adopts Felix, a stray dog found at the burned hub's fence line, and stands with Ilya at the ocean. The ghost of row twelve finally rests; what remains is chosen family and hard-won peace. Beat: quiet, complete closure.
